data.title: Allan Bødskov Andersen Appointed Chief Financial Officer of Bavarian Nordic
data.description:
Allan Bødskov Andersen

COPENHAGEN, Denmark, November 27, 2026 – Bavarian Nordic A/S OMX:BAVA today announced the appointment of Allan Bødskov Andersen as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and member of Executive Management, joining latest June 2027 succeeding Henrik Juuel, whose departure was recently announced.

Allan joins Bavarian Nordic from Topsoe, a global technology leader driving the clean energy transition currently serving as Group CFO and member of Executive Management, with responsibility for Global Finance, IT and Facility Management. Prior to Topsoe, Allan served as Group CFO at DLF and spent 16 years at Ørsted in several senior financial leadership positions, including CFO of the Onshore business and Head of Investor Relations. During his tenure at Ørsted, he played an important role in the company's IPO and gained extensive experience in capital markets, M&A and strategic investments.

Tarja Stenvall, President and CEO of Bavarian Nordic, said: “I am delighted to welcome Allan to Bavarian Nordic. He brings a strong strategic mindset, extensive CFO experience across industries and a deep understanding of how finance can partner with the business to drive performance and sustainable growth. In addition to his financial and capital markets expertise, I particularly value his collaborative and empowering leadership style, and his strong commitment to developing people and teams. I look forward to working closely with Allan as we shape the next chapter of Bavarian Nordic.”

Allan Bødskov Andersen said: “Bavarian Nordic has in recent years transformed into a leading global vaccine company with a proven manufacturing, supply chain and commercial platform, supported by a solid financial foundation. I am excited to join Bavarian Nordic at this important stage in the company’s development and look forward to contributing to its continued success and long-term value creation.”

About Allan Bødskov Andersen

With more than 25 years of experience in both the private and public sectors, Allan has an extensive background in treasury, funding, capital planning, risk management, insurance, and investor relations. Before joining Topsoe, Allan was the Group CFO of DLF Group and served as CFO Onshore and Head of Investor Relations at Ørsted, where he had been part of the finance division since 2006 and was responsible for the financial aspects of wind, solar and energy storage projects in Europe, US, and Asia. Prior to joining Ørsted, he served as Advisor at the central bank of Denmark. Allan holds an M.Sc. in Economics and Econometrics from the University of Southampton, UK, and a Ph.D. in Finance from the University of Aarhus, Denmark. He is member of the boards of Green2x A/S and Cavendish Hydrogen ASA. He is a Danish national, born in 1972.

About Bavarian Nordic

Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. For more information, visit www.bavarian-nordic.com

data.title: Paratus Energy: Q3 2026 Results
data.description:
HAMILTON, Bermuda, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Paratus Energy Services Ltd. (OSLO: PLSV) ("Paratus" or the "Company") today reported operational and financial results for the third quarter of 2026, highlighted by $79 million in combined segment revenues and $50 million in adjusted EBITDA, from continuing operations. The Company and its ownership in Seagems ended the quarter with $169 million in cash and a net debt of $239 million (1.3x leverage).

Paratus is pleased to announce that its Board of Directors (the "Board") has authorized a quarterly cash distribution of $0.22 per share for Q3 2026, consistent with prior quarters.

Q3 2026 highlights, including notable post-quarter developments:

  • Recently announced a strategic review of the Company's investment in the Seagems JV.
  • Successfully completed the Fontis sale and used cash proceeds received at closing towards partial redemption of bonds.
  • Delivered strong operational performance, with PLSV fleet technical utilization of approximately 99%.
  • Reported combined segment revenue and EBITDA of $79 million and $50 million, respectively.
  • Closed the quarter with combined cash of $169 million and net debt of $239 million (1.3x net leverage ratio).
  • Seagems was recently awarded a four-year contract for the third-party horizontal pipelaying vessel Safira.
  • Petrobras recently confirmed the acceptance of Seagems' bid for a four-year contract for Jade.
  • Post Q3, declared $0.22 per share dividend for Q3 2026, consistent with previous quarters.

Corporate and operational review for the third quarter of 2026

Strategic review of investment in the Seagems JV

On November 18, 2026, Paratus announced a strategic review of its investment in Seagems. Paratus and Vantris Energy Berhad ("Vantris") are conducting the review on a coordinated basis and exploring third-party interest in the Seagems business as a whole.

Pareto Securities is acting as financial adviser to Paratus, while J.P. Morgan is acting as financial adviser to Vantris. The review may or may not lead to a transaction, and no decision to transact has been taken by either of the two joint venture parties at this stage.

The Company will provide further updates as appropriate and in accordance with its disclosure obligations under applicable law.

Seagems operating and financial update

Paratus' 50% share in the Seagems joint venture contributed $78.6 million in contract revenues, compared with $71 million in the prior quarter. The quarter-over-quarter increase was primarily driven by the recovery from planned maintenance activities and operational incidents involving Esmeralda and Jade during the prior quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $51.1 million, up from $43.5 million in the prior quarter.

The JV achieved technical utilization of 98.6% (Q2 2026: 93.7%) and the contract backlog at quarter-end was approximately $0.9 billion (Q2 2026: approximately $1.1 billion), excluding the subsequent Safira award.

During the quarter, Seagems distributed $34.8 million to Paratus (Q2 2026: $30.2 million).

Earlier in 2026, Petrobras launched a PLSV tender for contracts commencing in 2028, comprising five lots with varying technical specifications and offering contract durations of four years. Seagems submitted bids for the Jade and a third-party vessel to which it had secured exclusive access in the event of a contract award.

On November 17, 2026, the Company announced that Seagems had been awarded a four-year contract with Petrobras for the third-party horizontal pipelaying vessel Safira, which is currently under construction. The contract is expected to commence in Q4 2028 and is expected to add approximately $410 million to Seagems' backlog, of which the Company has a 50% share.

Seagems has secured access to the vessel through a memorandum of understanding ("MOU"), which includes a purchase option. While the timing remains subject to change, Seagems currently expects to conclude on whether to acquire the vessel before year-end or early next year. If acquired, Safira would become the seventh owned vessel in Seagems' fleet and be expected to contribute significant operating cash flow once operations under the Petrobras contract commence.

Safira will have a horizontal pipelaying system ("HLS") with 300-tonne tension capacity. The Company believes that Safira is unlikely to target the more technically demanding, higher-tension deepwater projects that the high-specification 550-tonne PLSVs with vertical pipelaying systems (VLS) in Seagems' existing fleet are well suited for. Due to differences in vessel dimensions, tonnage, equipment configuration and operational capabilities, Safira's estimated construction cost is materially lower than the estimated replacement cost of Seagems' existing high-specification 550-tonne PLSVs.

The JV continues to explore opportunities to expand the Seagems business and leverage its established operational platform. This work is ongoing, and the Company believes that there is meaningful potential for further growth.

On November 9, 2026, the Company announced that Petrobras had published its final tender results, confirming the acceptance of Seagems' bid for the Jade PLSV. The prospective four-year contract is expected to commence in Q1 2028 and remains subject to formal award by Petrobras and the execution of definitive agreements. While no firm agreements are in place, we currently expect that the vessel will be employed during the time between the expiration of the current contract and the start-up of the prospective four-year contract with Petrobras.

Market outlook

On November 23, 2026, Petrobras announced its 2027-2031 business plan, providing for total capital expenditure of $122 billion, approximately 12% above the $109 billion included in its 2026-2030 plan. E&P remains the principal investment area, accounting for more than 70% of planned expenditure. The plan also indicates estimated demand for approximately 7,000 km of rigid and flexible pipelines and umbilicals, including installations and recoveries, compared with approximately 6,000 km in the previous plan. Overall, we believe the increased investment and activity levels are supportive of the demand outlook for subsea support vessels, including PLSVs, in Brazil.

Webcast

Paratus will host a presentation of the Q3 2026 results via an audio webcast today at 15:00 CET. To join the webcast, please use the following link:

https://paratusenergy.engagestream.euronext.com/q3-2026

For further information, please contact:

Baton Haxhimehmedi, CFO and Interim CEO

Baton.Haxhimehmedi@paratus-energy.com

+47 4063 9083

About Paratus

Paratus Energy Services Ltd. (OSLO: PLSV) is an investment holding company with a 50% joint venture interest in Seagems. Seagems is a leading subsea services company that owns and operates a fleet of six multi-purpose pipe-laying support vessels, providing support, installation, flexible pipe-laying and construction services. All vessels are currently operating under contracts in Brazil.

data.title: Nvidia, neoclouds in focus as chip sellers rule out Chinese renters
data.description:
Neoclouds are being told they won’t be able to purchase Nvidia chips if any of the computing capacity will be rented by Chinese companies, sources told CNBC.

It comes after a new rule restricting remote access to artificial-intelligence semiconductors was announced by the Trump administration on Nov. 16.

Chip sellers communicated the messaging to neoclouds after the announcement, which seeks to close an export controls loophole allowing Chinese companies to rent access to Nvidia’s most advanced chips when hosted in data centers overseas, the report said.

U.S.-listed neocloud stocks include CoreWeave , Nebius Group , IREN , Applied Digital , TeraWulf , Cipher Digital , Hut 8 , Core Scientific , and WhiteFiber

The interim final rule was reported by the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, and came into effect on Nov. 19. Previously imposed export controls have effectively banned the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies and their import into China.

Before the new rule’s announcement, Nvidia had said it would not sell its chips to customers renting more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies.

The new rule impacts the full supply chain, from the companies selling Nvidia chips to the neoclouds who rent access to computing power. Neocloud stocks have come under renewed pressure lately as investors questioned the sustainability of the AI boom.

The change has prompted Nvidia chip sellers to look for new buyers of the semiconductor giant’s GPUs, CNBC reported on Wednesday. Chip sellers were reportedly seeking to offload GPUs because they were originally for use in data centers through which Chinese companies would rent access.

data.description:

(06:10 GMT) *Thales Will Late File a Mandatory Simplified Tender Offer for All Lumibird Shares
(06:47 GMT) Thales Enters Talks for Majority Stake in Laser Maker Lumibird in $483 Million Deal

By Adam Whittaker

France's Thales said it is in exclusive talks to buy a majority stake in laser technologies company Lumibird, in a deal that would value the target's photonics division at around 440 million euros, including debt, equivalent to $482.6 million.

The aerospace-and-defense group said Friday that it plans to buy a 51.6% stake in Lumibird from its Chief Executive Officer and majority shareholder Marc Le Flohic. Thales said the deal values Lumibird at 30.10 euros a share. Lumibird shares closed Thursday at 24.55 euros. Thales expects to complete the deal in the second quarter of next year.

The price per share paid could rise to 32.66 euros, depending on the completion of the sale of Lumibird's medical division.

Thales said the deal would help create a European photonics platform and help it develop laser-directed energy weapons.

The company will later file a tender offer for all Lumibird shares that it doesn't hold and expects to complete this in the second half of 2027, it said.

data.title: USDJPY: Dollar Holds Above ¥159 as Tokyo Inflation Keeps BOJ Hike in Play
data.description:
Key points:
  • Tokyo core inflation reaches 2.9%
  • US yields keep the dollar supported
  • ¥160 puts intervention in focus

Japan’s accelerating core inflation strengthens the case for further tightening, but firm US yields leave the yen struggling to gain ground.

💴 Yen struggles despite hotter inflation

  • The pair traded around ¥159.25–¥159.35 early Friday, with the dollar retaining a modest advantage after Tokyo’s inflation release.
  • The figures supported expectations of another Bank of Japan rate increase, but stopped short of delivering the upside surprise that might have prompted a stronger yen rally.
  • Tokyo core consumer prices rose 2.9% annually in November, accelerating from 2.6% in October to a 16-month high. The reading nevertheless missed the 3% consensus forecast.
  • Japan’s core measure excludes fresh food but includes energy, making that distinction important when assessing the underlying inflation signal. Inflation excluding both fresh food and energy eased to 2.5% from 2.6%.

🏦 Two central banks keep traders guessing

  • The BOJ’s December 17–18 meeting is the next major domestic policy test. An increase remains the most likely move.
  • On the other end, the dollar has substantial support of its own. Markets are almost fully pricing a quarter-point Fed increase in December, while the US 10-year Treasury yield has climbed toward 4.89%.
  • A BOJ hike may offer limited relief if US rate expectations rise alongside it. A more durable yen recovery would become easier if Japanese tightening coincided with easing US yields or a less aggressive Fed outlook.

📊 ¥160 keeps traders on alert

  • The ¥160 area remains the immediate psychological reference above the market. Its proximity keeps intervention concerns relevant, but it is not an automatic trigger for official action.
  • Below the market, ¥159 is the nearest round-number reference. Holding above it would preserve the immediate upward bias; sustained trading underneath would indicate buyers losing momentum.
  • Friday’s shortened US session adds a liquidity complication. The pair enters that stretch caught between supportive dollar yields, Japan’s inflation pressure and the possibility of a sharper official response to yen weakness.

data.title: Swiggy's Instamart to layoff 340 employees amid AI transition, says report
data.description:
Artificial Intelligence and its role in taking over employment opportunities and resulting layoffs are gathering pace at an extensive pace.

SWIGGY LAYOFFS

Swiggy's quick delivery/quick commerce arm, Instamart, is set to fire 340 of its employees. As per a report from Moneycontrol, the company, which has lagged behind its competitors, Zomato's Blinkit and Zepto, among others, is planning to lay off 340 employees in its quick-commerce division as it restructures the business for its next stage of growth amid increased adoption of AI.

The report also pointed out that the move comes as competition intensifies, with Eternal-owned Blinkit, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and other players vying for market share. Swiggy, however, remains well capitalised, with approximately Rs 13,500 crore in cash and cash equivalents.

SAP TO FIRE 10,000

This report of layoffs comes on the same day Bloomberg reported that SAP SE is developing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 jobs as the German software company reshapes its business for an artificial intelligence transition.

The proposed reductions would affect at least 9% of SAP’s global workforce, though the final figure has yet to be determined.

The restructuring is expected to span several departments, including product and engineering, as well as sales. SAP is also revamping how it develops and markets its products as CEO Christian Klein advances an AI-focused strategy.

SWIGGY Q2 RESULTS 

Swiggy posted a smaller net loss in the September quarter, while revenue rose sharply across its businesses. Both food delivery and quick commerce delivered year-on-year growth.

The company recorded a net loss of ₹922 crore in Q2 FY27, down from ₹1,092 crore in the same quarter a year earlier, a reduction of nearly 16%.

Revenue from operations increased 54.4% year on year to ₹5,561 crore, compared with ₹3,601 crore in the year-ago period. This growth reflects ongoing expansion in Swiggy’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses.

Data showed that profit gains were concentrated in technology-related sectors, while consumer-facing manufacturers and construction companies logged losses during the period.

data.title: China stocks, yuan rally after Beijing vows stronger market support
data.description:
China's share benchmarks jumped more than 3% and the yuan reversed early losses on Friday, after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market.

China's benchmark Shanghai Composite Index and the blue-chip CSI300 index soared in afternoon trading, putting them on track for their best session in two years.

China's tech-focused STAR 50 Index surged 12%.

In Beijing's strongest gesture yet to support a stock market that had fallen to 16-month lows, the cabinet said "capital markets were crucial to the broader economy," adding that Central Huijin would enhance its role as a quasi-stabilisation fund to ensure ample liquidity, state media Xinhua reported.

The meeting also called for better policies to encourage long-term funds to invest in the stock market, and for measures to strengthen defences against risks spilling over from overseas markets.

"It's a shot in the arm for markets," said Kenny Ng, a strategist at Everbright Securities International in Hong Kong.

"Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south."

The CSI Semiconductor Industry Index (.CSI931865)，the STAR Chip Index (.STARCHIP) both shot up more than 16%.

Indices tracking China's AI , cloud computing (.CSI930851) and consumer electronics stocks (.CSI931494) jumped more than 10%.

Everbright's Ng added that the meeting sent a clear signal that regulators do not want to see the market slide further, but cautioned that future market trends would be decided by many other factors including US-China relations, tariffs on trade, and chip supply following tighter US restrictions.

The rally also spread to Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index gained 2% while the Hang Seng Tech Index (.HSETCH) jumped 6%.

data.title: India urges states to sign 41 GW of pending clean power contracts
data.description:
India's federal government urged states on Friday to sign more contracts for 41 gigawatts (GW) of clean energy capacity that has no buyers.

States need to identify their power requirements well in advance and sign more battery storage contracts along with clean energy, Shripad Naik, union minister of state for power and new and renewable energy, said at the State Power Ministers Conference in New Delhi.

  • The lack of battery energy storage resulted in states scrambling for power to meet their evening and night demand as the El Nino weather pattern pushed up consumption this year

  • The unexpected surge in demand strained India's power system in September and October despite the country having surplus solar energy, Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said at the conference

  • Peak power demand of 271 GW in May was 11.6% higher than a year earlier, Agarwal said

  • "There were days we could barely meet their evening peak demand despite having surplus clean energy during the day," Agarwal said

  • Naik also urged states to speed up payments tied to the acquisition of land for transmission projects, saying slow payments have led to huge delays

  • Insufficient transmission capacity has forced India to curtail renewable power generation, which has wasted clean energy

data.title: UK's Dolphin Drilling Q3 revenue falls on rig transition, demobilization costs
data.description:
Overview

  • UK offshore rig operator's Q3 revenue declined, impacted by rig transition and demobilization costs

  • Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 was nearly flat compared to Q2, reflecting rig preparation costs

  • Net loss widened in Q3, including $3.5 mln currency loss and transition expenses

Outlook

  • Both owned rigs scheduled to be on long-term contracts from December 2026

  • Company expects 2027 to have both owned rigs on contract for the full year

  • Company says tight supply and strong demand for moored semi-submersibles support strategy

Result Drivers

  • RIG PREPARATION AND DEMOBILISATION COSTS - Q3 results were affected by $6.3 mln of costs to prepare Borgland Dolphin for contract and $1 mln in Blackford Dolphin demobilisation costs

  • ASSET SALE IMPACT - Sale of Blackford Dolphin reduced operating costs and eliminated future capital expenditure for the rig

  • CAPITAL-LIGHT STRATEGY - Joint venture with SPM provides a platform for growth in rig management without significant capital investment

data.title: Imperial Brands Stock Up On Altria's Confirmation Of Possible Takeover Offer
data.description:
HENRICO COUNTY (dpa-AFX) - Shares of Imperial Brands PLC (IMBBY.PK, IMB.L) climbed around 15 percent on Thursday's London trading after U.S. tobacco major Altria Group, Inc. (MO) confirmed a possible takeover offer for the British peer.

Meanwhile, responding to Altria's statement, Imperial Brands said its Board has not had any discussions with, or received any approach or proposal from, Altria or the third party referenced.

Earlier in the day, Altria Group issued a statement in response to recent press speculation, confirming that it is considering a possible offer for Imperial Brands. Any offer, if made, is likely to be solely in cash.

Altria confirmed that it is also in discussions with a third party regarding its possible acquisition of part of the business of Imperial Brands.

However, the companies have not reached any agreement so far. There can be no certainty that an offer will ultimately be made nor as to the terms on which any offer may be made, it said.

Altria is required to announce a firm intention to make an offer for Imperial Brands by no later than December 24, or that it does not intend to make an offer.

Following the news, Imperial Brands said its Board is clear in its duty of aiming to maximise shareholder value and will consider any proposal, should one be made. The firm also urged shareholders not to take any action at this time.

Imperial Brands added that it has strong confidence in its strategy and trading.

On November 17, Imperial Brands reported a drop in pre-tax income and revenue for fiscal 2026, and said it expects fiscal 2027 adjusted operating profit to grow at a similar level to fiscal 2026, on a constant currency basis, primarily driven by continued profit growth from the company's combustible tobacco business.

While reporting the results, the firm also had announced planned job cuts as part of its transformation strategy, which is estimated to generate cost savings of at least 320 million pounds per annum by 2030.

In fiscal year 2026, the company projects reduction of 2,100 roles globally. Additionally, the Bristol-based company plans for a further reduction of between 2,100 and 2,500 roles by the end of 2030.

In London, Imperial Brands shares closed Thursday's trading at 3,432.00 pence, up 14.85 percent.

In the overnight activity on the NYSE, Altria shares were trading 0.33 percent lower at $76.03, after closing Thursday's regular trading 1.95 percent higher.
